messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D decreased linearly from controls to at-risk individuals to those with full-threshold MDD.
Sentence: "A linear increase of inflammatory markers (CRP P=0.026; IL-6 P=0.090), cortisol (P=0.025) and decrease of vitamin D (P<0.001) was found across the entire sample (for example, from controls to those at risk and those with full-threshold MDD)."
Measured as: MDD status across controls, at-risk and full-threshold MDD (vitamin D as marker)
Population: 230 controls and 2333 participants at risk for or with MDD, aged 18-65 (NESDA)
Intervention: Measured vitamin D level (observational)
Comparator: Controls versus at-risk versus full-threshold MDD
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 2,563
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: Vitamin D level was significantly related to risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5) six months after COVID-19 hospital admission; the direction is not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "The variables that were significantly related to the risk of depression 6 months after admission for COVID-19 were frailty (p = 0.006 for pre-frail and p = 0.001 for frail), small-vessel vascular disease in imaging tests (p = 0.033), vitamin D level (p = 0.006), and taking antidepressants (p = 0.011)."
Measured as: risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5)
Population: 72 patients admitted to a hospital in Spain for COVID-19, assessed at discharge and six months later
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A is a large cross-sectional association with vitamin D as a marker, while Study B is a small cohort where vitamin D is one of several risk variables in COVID-19 patients; the populations and designs differ and Study B's direction is unstated.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["design_or_bias"],"detail":"population: NESDA community/at-risk adults (n = 2,563) vs 72 hospitalized COVID-19 patients; design: cross-sectional vs small cohort"}
